reviews.author: inaneswine
reviews.content:
There are films that are so bad they’re good. Then there are films that are simply bad. And then, right at the bottom of the barrel, there are films that aren’t merely bad but deeply offensive. *Ice Cream Man* is what Eli Roth has scraped from beneath that barrel.

Remember *Hostel*? One of Roth’s earliest films, it caused such a furore that it helped popularise an entire subgenre: “torture porn”. Yet, for all its reputation, Roth actually demonstrated considerable restraint. Some of its most frightening moments occur precisely when the camera turns away from the violence.

His subsequent films—including *Hostel: Part II*, *The Green Inferno* and *Knock Knock*—suggested a steady erosion of that restraint and a descent into gleeful gore, obnoxious provocation and increasingly cringeworthy camp.

There is plenty of all three in *Ice Cream Man*, and that is not necessarily a problem. Gore and camp can be enormously entertaining when handled with wit, imagination or technical skill. Here, however, everything is executed so artlessly that the film quickly becomes numbing. The effects look fake, the dialogue is juvenile, and the characters are little more than bodies waiting to be dissected. The performances are uniformly amateurish, from adults and children alike. Even allowing for the leeway usually afforded to young actors, it is painfully apparent that Roth has no idea how to direct them. Nothing is shocking because nothing feels consequential. It is simply boring.

The film never finds a workable pace or tone. It lurches constantly between idiotic adults walking willingly towards their deaths, extreme close-ups of mutilation and tedious scenes in which the child protagonists recite dialogue so insipid that it sounds as though they wrote it themselves—although that is probably an insult to child writers.

One character, temporarily paralysed, spends what feels like two solid minutes flopping from room to room like a landed fish. Whatever comic potential the sequence initially possesses is exhausted long before the scene ends.

All of that would be disappointing enough. What makes *Ice Cream Man* genuinely enraging, however, is its relentless parade of offensive ideas masquerading as transgressive humour.

A young woman is forced to promise that she will reconcile with her ex-boyfriend before he agrees to rescue her—and then she actually does. Paedophilia becomes the premise for a ludicrous comedy-horror that never comes close to establishing a coherent tone. A protagonist casually uses the ableist R-slur before another character turns autism into the punchline of the very next joke.

In one grotesquely misjudged sequence, a Black person is chained to the back of a truck and dragged along the ground, invoking the imagery of racist violence and lynching, seemingly in pursuit of one more cheap shock.

But the pièce de résistance—the final insult, the cherry on top, if you’ll pardon the pun—is the moment when a child actor, in a film released in 2026, is made to utter the following appalling line:

> “I’m a 12-year-old girl. Of course I know how to throw up.”

At that moment, it took everything I had not to get up and walk straight out of the cinema.

Even by the low standards Roth has increasingly set for himself, *Ice Cream Man* is a disgrace. It is a film that mistakes misogyny for edginess, ableism for humour, and racist imagery for entertainment. Beneath all the gore and desperate provocation, there is no intelligence, no daring and no discernible humanity—just an ugly, witless film congratulating itself for having the nerve to be offensive.

reviews.author: KieranFreemantle
reviews.content:
I was hoping *Ice Cream Man* would be a fun piece of schlock, and there was some of that in the film. Sadly, *Ice Cream Man* was a one-joke movie that rammed it hard into the ground. Eli Roth's mean-spirited nature was present in the film, and it felt uncomfortable watching very young children commit violent acts, and a joke involving a 12-year-old girl's eating disorder.

Also, fuck generative AI!\

reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: Oh, now come on - who hasn't enjoyed delicious Mint Romney ice cream? Unfortunately, there is a side effect if you feed it to our children - it turns them into marauding murderers intent on killing every adult they see whether they be parent, guardian, granny or teacher. Luckily, though, "Jared" (Charlie Zelzter) is lactose intolerant and his sister "Lizzie" (Sarah Abbott) won't let him have any. Phew! That leaves him, "Mia" (Kiori Mirza Waldman) and "Tommy" (Shiloh O'Reilly) as the only kids in the town not determined on a rampage of gory slaughter. What's causing all of this? Well they (and we) quickly deduce that it must have something to do with the creepy ice cream man (Ari Millen) whose van appears at all hours of the day and night to top up their dose of coned-delights and so fuel their antics - even the hunky fireman isn't safe! After about ten minutes, this descended into a most puerile and unsophisticated dose of CGI-driven nonsense that did, at least, invoke a degree of unanimity from the dozen or so of us in the cinema who were all looking at each other wondering how this ever got off the drawing board. It's repetitious; there's no jeopardy nor is there even the vaguest attempt to craft any characters that we might care less about as their killing spree finds as many ways of carving someone up and then sets it all to music. It's as if Messrs. Belson and Roth just typed the word kill into a digital thesaurus and then let their computers run riot with the results. To be fair to Zeltzer, he tries to inject a little stoic humanity in to the proceedings - even if his some of his riper dialogue uses language that people his own age wouldn't be able to sit on the other side of the screen and actually watch; but the remainder of the cast just look like they've been just been told to go make some mess for the cameras. Even Hammer or John Carpenter at their abject worst managed to keep us interested in what was happening to some extent, but this really hasn't anything to redeem it at all - except perhaps the end credits. It smacks of something that someone might think has legs for another scoop, but I really hope those with the cash take a stance against such auto-trash and invest in cinema that actually requires people to screw up rather than just our machines.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: An idyllic summer town devolves into terror when a sinister ice cream man begins distributing horrifying, twisted treats to the local children.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: In a quiet, picturesque summer town, local children eagerly gather around the neighborhood ice cream truck to beat the heat. However, the seemingly friendly ice cream man hides a disturbing secret, using his sweet confections to inflict gruesome consequences on unsuspecting kids. As strange occurrences and horrifying incidents begin to multiply, panic spreads among the terrified residents. A small group of youth must uncover the chilling truth behind the truck's deadly frozen treats before the entire community is consumed by madness.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Life in a peaceful suburban town seems picture-perfect as warm weather brings children running into the streets at the familiar chime of the local ice cream truck. Beneath the cheerful surface, however, the enigmatic vendor is harboring malicious intentions and serving treats infused with nightmarish secret ingredients. As children start experiencing horrifying transformations and terrifying symptoms, the town's initial sense of safety rapidly collapses into widespread hysteria. Distraught parents and local authorities struggle to make sense of the sudden, surreal emergencies, entirely unaware of the villain operating in plain sight. Meanwhile, an observant teenager begins noticing terrifying patterns connecting the ice cream man's route to the sudden outbreak of madness. Driven by desperation to protect their friends, a small group of determined youth band together to investigate the vendor's sinister origin and secretive workshop. Their harrowing search uncovers a grisly operation fueled by dark, unnatural ingredients and twisted malice. Confronting the madman in a desperate bid to stop the carnage, the kids must face unimaginable horrors to dismantle his cruel enterprise. Ultimately, the fight for survival exposes the deep vulnerability of their once-safe neighborhood, leaving a chilling legacy that changes the town forever.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Set against the backdrop of a sun-drenched summer, Ice Cream Man delves into the sinister collapse of an idyllic suburban community. When a strange vendor arrives offering colorful, delicious frozen desserts, he quickly becomes a favorite among the local youth. But behind his warm smile and lively truck bells lies a dark, macabre agenda. The sweet confections soon yield horrifying effects, thrusting unsuspecting families into a nightmare of dread, mystery, and gruesome terror. Blending elements of suspenseful horror and poignant drama, this tale explores how fragile normalcy can be when absolute evil hides behind the most innocent of childhood joys.

story_structure.climax: The escalating madness reaches a breaking point in a town-wide confrontation, forcing the remaining sane residents to face the full terror of the ice cream man's ultimate plot.
story_structure.conflict: The town's perfect facade begins to crack as the ice cream man's treats produce increasingly bizarre, unsettling, and horrifying effects on the kids who consume them.
story_structure.resolution: The immediate threat is dealt with, leaving the scarred town to pick up the pieces of their shattered community while grappling with the lingering paranoia of what transpired.
story_structure.introduction: An idyllic summer town is introduced, enjoying the warmth and the arrival of a seemingly friendly ice cream man who serves sweet delights to the neighborhood children.
story_structure.risingAction: Suspicion grows among a few observant residents as the town descends further into madness, strange occurrences multiply, and the true, sinister nature of the ice cream man begins to surface.
